column1: # Akruti Kannada glyph table: AkrutiKndPadma and its Bold, Demi and Demib weights,
# The format is described in src/legacy/table.rs. Codes are Windows-1252 bytes.
# Derived from documents, as no code page is published. The glyphs were rendered
# from the Akruti fonts embedded in public Karnataka PDFs: the full
# AkrutiKndPadmaDemi0100 and AkrutiKndPadmaBold0100 programs in the Kannada Acts
# on dpal.kar.nic.in, made with PageMaker 6.52 and Acrobat Distiller 5.0, where each
# glyph's name G<n> gives its code n, and the TrueType subsets in the 2002 budget
# highlights bh2002k.pdf (kar.nic.in/finance/bud2002-kan/), whose codes are the
# bytes the page shows. Each glyph was identified by eye and matched against
# glyphs shaped with HarfBuzz from Kannada Sangam MN and Noto Sans Kannada, then
# checked in context: 16,857 lines of Akruti text in 33 Acts and Ordinances of 2001
# to 2003 and the 2002 budget highlights and speech, all fetched from the Internet
# Archive, were converted and every unknown glyph and malformed syllable was read
# against the page image. Bold and Demi draw the same letter at every code.
# docs/akruti.md has the method and results.
# Codes the fonts have but no document used are left out, and are reported as
# unknown: 2A, 6A, A1, A2, A3, A6, A7, A8, B4, BF, E0, E1, E3, EC, ED, F0.
# Consonants drawn without the head stroke
# Consonants built from 2 or 3 glyphs: ಮ from ವ, ಯ from a base of its own
# Vowel signs. E2 is the head stroke for the inherent a.
# Typists often put a space (20, or the no-break space A0) before ೃ, ೖ and the
# subscripts ಯ and ಮ, which draw under the glyph before them. After a syllable, the space
# ೆ with the ೃ glyph under it reads as ೈ: ವೆೃರ್ is typed for ವೈರ್.
